name: High-dimensional dynamics of generalization error in neural networks
summary: Analyses gradient descent in linear and shallow networks with random matrix theory, and finds overtraining worst when the effective number of parameters equals the number of examples.

name: Reconciling modern machine learning practice and the bias-variance trade-off
summary: Names the double descent risk curve and shows it for random Fourier features, two-layer networks, random forests and boosting on MNIST and other datasets.

name: A U-turn on Double Descent: Rethinking Parameter Counting in Statistical Learning
summary: Argues that double descent in trees, boosting and linear regression comes from switching between two complexity axes, and that effective parameter counts restore U shapes.

name: Surprises in High-Dimensional Ridgeless Least Squares Interpolation
summary: Derives the asymptotic risk of minimum-norm least squares and ridge regression when the number of features and samples grow together, and recovers double descent in linear and random-feature models.

name: A Brief Prehistory of Double Descent
summary: A letter that traces double descent in minimum-norm linear classifiers back to Vallet et al. (1989), Opper et al. (1990) and Duin (2000).

name: Deep Double Descent: Where Bigger Models and More Data Hurt
summary: Shows model-wise, epoch-wise and sample-wise double descent in CNNs, ResNets and Transformers, and defines effective model complexity.

name: Optimal Regularization Can Mitigate Double Descent
summary: Proves that optimally tuned ridge regularization makes the test risk monotone in sample size and model size for isotropic linear regression, and shows the same effect empirically for networks.

name: Double Descent Demystified: Identifying, Interpreting & Ablating the Sources of a Deep Learning Puzzle
summary: Explains double descent in ordinary linear regression by three factors that must all be present, and removes it by ablating each factor on real data.
